notes: The MKR WiFi 1010 is not in the catalogue, so a new part type was created from the pin labels in the diagram (AREF, A0-A6, 0-14, 5V, VIN, VCC, GND, RESET).
The image shows the board's top-left pin labelled DAC0/A0. I named it A0.
The breadboard image labels the upper half as rows j-f. The catalogue puts rows f-j in bank 'b', so I used '<col>b.<row>' names for those holes. Columns are read off the image.

Resistor: columns 3 and 6, row h. LED: columns 6 and 8, row i. Green wire: board pin 2 to 3b.g, which shares a strip with the resistor leg in column 3. Black wire: board GND to 8b.h, which shares a strip with the LED cathode.

LED polarity: the bent (longer) leg is the anode, in the resistor's column 6. The straight leg is the cathode, in column 8, which goes to GND. This matches the schematic: pin 2, then resistor, then LED, then GND.
The Micro USB cable is in the parts list but not drawn. I added it as a joined edge to the board with no port names, because the usb-cable catalogue entry has no ports.
The breadboard power rails are not used.
The analog pin A1 read in the code uses nothing external. The tutorial wires only the LED circuit.
